segments.he: רַבָּה מְטַלְטֵל לְהוּ אַגַּב לָקָנָא דְמַיָּא. רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עָבֵיד לְהוּ כִּגְרָף שֶׁל רֶיעִי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רֶיעִי לְכַתְּחִילָּה?
segments.en: «Rabba would move them along with a pitcher of water. Rav Huna, son» of «Rav Yehoshua, would render them a chamber pot with excrement.» The Sages permitted moving repulsive vessels. Here, too, he would collect all the date pits and then move them out because they were disgusting. «Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: And may one create a chamber pot with excrement ab initio?» Although the Sages permitted moving a container of excrement, they did not permit creating one ab initio so that it would be permitted to move it.

segments.he: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת זָרֵיק לְהוּ בְּלִישָּׁנֵיהּ. רַב פָּפָּא זָרֵיק לְהוּ אֲחוֹרֵי הַמִּטָּה. אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן אַבְקוּלָס שֶׁהָיָה מַחֲזִיר פָּנָיו אֲחוֹרֵי הַמִּטָּה וְזוֹרְקָן.
segments.en: «Rav Sheshet would dispose of» the pits «with his tongue. Rav Pappa would dispose of them behind the divan» on which he sat while eating because he did not want to move them in another manner. «They said about Rabbi Zekharya ben Avkolas that he would turn his face» toward the «back of the divan and dispose of them.»
